provenance_summary: V1-B biological expansion wave. Bacterial biosurfactants (rhamnolipid, surfactin) as bio-emulsifiers and adsorbents for oil-water separation and organic pollutant removal.

mechanisms.name: Biosurfactant emulsification
mechanisms.description: Biosurfactants reduce interfacial tension and emulsify oil droplets for oil-water separation

pollutant_feature.text: Oil and organic pollutants in water

bio_structure.text: Amphiphilic biosurfactant molecule (hydrophilic head + hydrophobic tail)

interaction.text: Reduces interfacial tension, emulsifies oil droplets

why_it_works.text: Amphiphilic structure enables oil-water interface modification

causal_chain.transferable_principle: Bacterial biosurfactants reduce interfacial tension for oil-water separation and organic pollutant removal

engineering_constraints.description: Biosurfactant production: microbial fermentation, yield depends on species and carbon source

narrative.text: Bacterial biosurfactants are amphiphilic molecules produced by microorganisms. Rhamnolipid (from Pseudomonas aeruginosa) and surfactin (from Bacillus subtilis) are the most studied. They reduce interfacial tension and can emulsify oil for water purification.

design_translation.idea: Produce biosurfactants via microbial fermentation and use for oil-water separation and organic pollutant removal
